text.p: Following are some major events which occurred on February 23 in history.
1447 - Eugenius IV, Pope from 1431, died. His reign was mostly taken up with a conflict with the Council of Basel which wished to institute reform.

1633 - Samuel Pepys, English diarist, born. His diary covered 1660 to 1669, with highlights his eyewitness accounts of the great plague which afflicted Britain and the subsequent Great Fire of London.
1685 - George Frederick Handel, German composer best known for his great choral work "Messiah", born. His vast output included operas, oratorios and many cantatas and other vocal music.
1744 - Meyer Amschel Rothschild, German founder of the banking dynasty, born.
1792 - Sir Joshua Reynolds, influential English portrait painter, died. He was first president of the Royal Academy.
1820 - The Cato Street Conspiracy, an attempt to assassinate British cabinet ministers, was discovered with hours to spare. The plotters were executed.

1821 - John Keats, English Romantic poet, died in Rome. Famed for his sensuous imagery. His work includes "On a Grecian Urn", "To a Nightingale" and "The Eve of St Agnes". He also wrote the epic "Hyperion".

1836 - General Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna with several thousand Mexican troops began besieging the Alamo mission settlement held by a force of 145 Texans led by Colonel Travis, Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. The siege ended on March 6 with all the Texans killed.
1848 - John Quincy Adams, sixth president of the United States, died.
1866 - King Alexander Cuza of Romania was forced to abdicate and was succeeded by Charles, Prince of Hohenzollern as Carol I.
1883 - Victor Fleming, U.S. film director, born. Best known for "The Wizard of Oz" and "Captains Courageous".
1898 - In France, novelist Emile Zola was imprisoned for writing his "J'accuse" letter accusing the government of anti-semitism and wrongly jailing Captain Alfred Dreyfus.
1905 - The Rotary Club was founded by lawyer Paul Percy Harris in Chicago.
1917 - Russians staged an enormous demonstration in Petrograd in protest against food shortages.
1919 - Benito Mussolini broke with the Socialist party and founded his own Fasci del Comattimento (Fascist) party in Italy.
1931 - Dame Nellie Melba (Helen Porter Mitchell), Australian operatic soprano, died. She had retired in 1926.
1934 - Sir Edward Elgar, English composer, died. His works included the oratorio "The Dream of Gerontius" , "Enigma Variations" and the "Pomp and Circumstance" marches.
1944 - Soviet dictator Josef Stalin forced one million Chechens into exile and dissolved the republic accusing them of collaboration with Nazi Germany.
1945 - The Japanese island of Iwo Jima fell to the Americans after severe fighting.
1965 - Stan Laurel, British-born half of the Laurel and Hardy comedy duo, died.
1970 - Guyana, formerly British Guiana, became an independent republic within the Commonwealth.
1981 - Lt-Col Antonio Tejero and a group of civil guards burst into the Spanish parliament firing shots in a failed coup attempt.
1991 - Thailand's armed forces seized power in a bloodless coup and arrested prime minister Chatichai Choonhaven.
1994 - Bosnia's government and separatist Bosnian Croat forces agreed a comprehensive ceasefire under U.N. auspices.
1994 - The Russian parliament voted to pardon participants in an armed rebellion against President Boris Yeltsin in October 1993 and a hardline Soviet coup attempt in 1991.
1996 - Pope John Paul issued an updated code for electing Popes, introducing modern comforts for cardinals in conclave and reaffirming rules against electronic bugging to safeguard their secrecy.
1996 - Two top-level Iraqi dissidents were murdered by relatives only days after returning home to a pardon from President Saddam Hussein.
